# PLAYBOOK: how the reference shorts handle each situation (generated from kit/reference/knowledge/rules.json; do not edit by hand)

READ THIS FIRST. These are HABITS measured and seen in real reference shorts. Learn the habit, do not copy a shot. A new topic needs its own world, props and
story; use the habit for how to show it. Each rule says [id | how sure]: measured = computed from every frame, seen = read by eye with the time given, inferred = reasoned, proposed = designed by an independent study, NOT verified by us (use as a starting value).
Use the SITUATIONS list: find the beat you are planning (hook, new place, key prop, dialogue, impact, ...) and follow its recipe and rule ids.

STATUS: the render code does not read these rules yet. This file is knowledge for Gemini and for people; a rule is an engine feature only when listed under ENGINE below.

Studied: pirate_cannonballs, memory_price, second_draw, mirror_horse_race, storm_oil, perfect_railroads, roller_coasters, town_button, vp3 (Japan pachinko hall), vp4 (lottery ticket), vp5 (two kingdoms and a blacksmith), slot_machines, winning_tickets, idea_zone, random_numbers, knight_loophole, grave_bell.

## What our videos do wrong now (measured against these references)
- 58 hard cuts per minute, references 2 to 15 (median 7)
- scene changes 28.3 per minute, references 16.0-24.9 (median 20.4): ours changes place somewhat too often (about 40 % above the median)
- every scene change is a hard cut (100 %); references: 43 % dissolve, 22 % camera fly-through, 21 % hard cut, 12 % in-place, 2 % whip
- 25 hard cuts per minute are angle cuts inside one scene; references median 1.1 per minute
- 78 % of shots are a pure zoom (push-in), references 0 to 7 %
- the same camera move repeats in the next shot 89 % of the time, references 0 to 63 % (median 33 %)
- camera moves are flat (parallax 0.27, references 0.32 to 0.44)
- flights are short (0.57 s, references 0.8 to 1.6 s) and the pauses between them are long (2.3 s, references 0.7 to 1.7 s)
- picture moves fast only 21 % of the time (references 27 to 54 %)
- surfaces: 60 % flat colour and 5.6 % gradient, references 35-48 % flat and 14-20 % gradient
- palette 23 colours (references 36 to 46); frame-to-frame change 0.6 to 2.6 (references 3.6 to 9.5)
- no captions in the picture (references: one word at a time, 100 % of the time)

## Rules

### CAMERA (how it moves, and why)
- [CAM-01 | measured | for: any] The camera is almost always alive, but not always flying. DO: Plan each beat as HOLD or FLIGHT. Flights run 27-54 % of the time, slow creep or stillness 20-51 %. The mix depends on the topic (see PRF-02). Never leave a long beat with a frozen camera and nothing else moving. NUMBERS: time_moving_fast 0.271-0.537 (median 0.4); time_nearly_still 0.205-0.507 (median 0.355); frames_with_almost_no_change 0-6 % of frames. SEEN IN: all 17 references. [applies: universal] (ours now: fast 21 %, still 43 %)
- [CAM-02 | measured | for: any] A flight is about one second long, one every 3 seconds, followed by a short hold. DO: Flight length 0.5-2.8 s, typical 1.1 s. One flight every 2-5 s (13-24 per minute). Hold between flights typically 0.7-1.7 s. Peak speed about 100 % of frame width per second (45-245). NUMBERS: flight_s p10 0.5 / p50 1.07 / p90 2.82; flights_per_min 13.06-24.22 (median 18.4); gap_s median per video 0.706-1.728; peak_px_per_frame p10 4.0 / p50 9.7 / p90 21.96. SEEN IN: 299 flights in 17 references. [applies: universal] (ours now: flight 0.57 s, pause 2.3 s)
- [CAM-03 | measured | for: any] Move the camera through the 3D world. Do not just zoom. DO: Every flight changes camera POSITION: orbit 20-60 degrees, crane up or down, dolly past objects, tilt while pushing. Foreground, subject and background must slide at different speeds (parallax). A pure push-in or pull-out with no pan, tilt or orbit is rare: use it for 0-7 % of shots. NUMBERS: pure_zoom_shots 0-7 % (median 0); parallax_ratio 0.322-0.438 (0 flat, 1 strong); shot_net_motion shots that combine a push or pull with a pan, tilt or orbit make up about 90 % of all shots (80-100 %). SEEN IN: pirate_cannonballs 0-1.2 s (orbit around the cannon, sea and island revealed); memory_price 4-7 s (fly down an alley into the shop). [applies: universal] (ours now: 78 % pure push-in, parallax 0.27)
- [CAM-04 | seen | for: new_place, explain_system] REVEAL: start tight on a detail or a face, then fly out, up or around until the place or its size is clear. DO: Frame 1: face or small object. Last frame: wide view with the hero object of the topic in it. Use crane-up or top-down to show layout or scale of a system. SEEN IN: town_button 4-7 s (crane up to a top view of the circular town); roller_coasters 1-3 s (tilt up the loop); mirror_horse_race 12-14 s (street and hill revealed). [applies: universal]
- [CAM-05 | seen | for: key_prop, action_impact] LAND ON THE PROP: a fast push toward the named prop that slows down as it arrives, timed to the word. DO: Start 0.3-0.5 s before the word, arrive on the word. End with the prop filling 40-100 % of the frame, readable. Ease: fast start, slow finish (decelerate). SEEN IN: second_draw 14-15 s (push to the gun while yellow streaks fly); town_button 23-25 s (button under the glass dome); memory_price 28-31 s (HAPPINESS gauge). [applies: universal]
- [CAM-06 | seen | for: danger, any] Power and danger: low angle, big object in the foreground. DO: Camera at ground height looking slightly up, holster or weapon or hull edge large and sharp in the lower third, subject behind. SEEN IN: second_draw 0-4 s (bullet and holster in the foreground, camera tilts up to the face). [applies: universal]
- [CAM-07 | seen | for: action_impact, danger] FOLLOW: when something travels, the camera pans or tracks with it and the background streams by. DO: Keep the mover in the same screen spot, let the background slide, constant speed. SEEN IN: mirror_horse_race 27-31 s (horse gallops, camera tracks); pirate_cannonballs 4-5 s (ball flies past). [applies: universal]
- [CAM-08 | seen | for: dialogue] Dialogue and reaction beats are HELD: two-shot or close-up, slow creep, 1.5-4 s. DO: Save the fast flights for reveals and impacts. Change only the faces and small props while the camera rests. SEEN IN: second_draw 9-13 s (four seconds on one medium shot); storm_oil 7-11 s (captain and chef two-shot). [applies: universal]
- [CAM-09 | measured | for: any] Ease every flight. Half are steady, a quarter ease in and out. DO: constant speed 50 % of flights (follow, long gentle drift). ease in and out 23 % (reveals). decelerate 8 % (landing on a prop). move then hold 7 %, varying 10 %. almost never accelerate. NUMBERS: ease_share {'accelerate': 0.0, 'constant': 0.52, 'decelerate': 0.07, 'ease_in_out': 0.25, 'hold_then_move': 0.0, 'move_then_hold': 0.06, 'varying': 0.09}. SEEN IN: 172 flights. [applies: universal] (ours now: 67 % constant, 22 % ease, 11 % accelerate)
- [CAM-10 | measured | for: any] Do not repeat the same move beat after beat. Vary push, pull, orbit, tilt, pan, top-down, low angle, first person. DO: Never more than two beats in a row with the same kind of move. Change camera height or angle at least every 2-3 s of flight time. NUMBERS: repeat_in_next_shot 0.0-0.633 in references (median 0.333), 0.89 in ours. SEEN IN: 8 references. [applies: universal] (ours now: 89 % repeat)
- [CAM-11 | seen | for: any] Use shot size as a language: tiny people in a wide world, medium two-shots, face close-ups, extreme close-ups of props. DO: Wide: people under 10 % of frame height, the world is the subject. Medium: people 35-50 % of frame height. Close-up: head 40-60 % of frame width. Insert: prop fills the frame. Change size at nearly every sentence. SEEN IN: pirate_cannonballs 0-20 s; memory_price 19-31 s. [applies: universal]
- [CAM-12 | seen | for: any] Frame with something blurred in the foreground at an edge (rope, pole, rail, mast, leaves) to build depth. DO: One soft foreground object on one side, subject sharp behind it. SEEN IN: perfect_railroads 14-17 s; pirate_cannonballs 12-14 s; roller_coasters 10-15 s. [applies: universal]
- [CAM-13 | seen | for: dialogue, introduce_character, number_data, explain_system] WHEN NOT TO MOVE: hold the camera when a person talks, thinks, reacts, or when a number or a rule is being read. WHY: The viewer needs a steady frame to read a face, a caption or a number. Moving the camera there competes with the information. DO: Hold 2-6 s (up to 10 s once) on one medium shot or close-up. Keep life in the frame while the camera rests: eyes, mouth, small gestures, light flicker, floating particles, a slow creep of 1-3 %. Move again at the next scene change or the next reveal. NUMBERS: time_nearly_still_per_video 0.205-0.507 (median 0.355); highest 0.53-0.54 in vp3 and vp4; frames_fully_held 0-6 % (something always moves). SEEN IN: idea_zone 0-10 s (one character on a chair under a lamp, almost still); vp5 0-6 s (king, blacksmith and anvil); random_numbers 15-23 s (clerk beside the elevator panel); vp4 3-8 s (clerk and customer at the counter). [applies: universal]
- [CAM-14 | measured | for: any] Shape every camera flight with a quick attack and a long, soft release. OBSERVED: Camera flights start already moving (about 40 % of peak speed in the first tenth), reach the peak about 38 % of the way through, then taper slowly. Ramp-up 0.28 s, ramp-down 0.47 s. WHY: A fast start keeps energy; a long ease-out lets the viewer land on the new framing. DO: Speed curve for a flight, 11 points from start to end as a share of peak speed: 0.39, 0.56, 0.65, 0.68, 0.68, 0.65, 0.61, 0.55, 0.45, 0.3, 0.13. Ramp-up (10 to 90 % of peak) 0.15-0.46 s, typical 0.28 s. Ramp-down 0.23-0.58 s, typical 0.47 s. Peak speed about 39-69 % of the frame width per second (median 54), measured as median pixel motion. NUMBERS: ramp_up_s 0.15-0.458 (median 0.28); ramp_down_s 0.226-0.582 (median 0.47); peak_pct_width_per_s 38.74-68.6 (median 54.2); peak_position_in_flight 0.266-0.498 (median 0.38); speed_curve_11_all [0.39, 0.56, 0.65, 0.68, 0.68, 0.65, 0.61, 0.55, 0.45, 0.3, 0.13]; flights 259. SEEN IN: 259 flights in 17 references. [applies: universal] (ours now: ramp-up 0.17 s, ramp-down 0.4 s, peak 45 % per second. Close, a little too abrupt at the start.)
- [CAM-15 | measured | for: any] Use depth of field at the frame edges (soft foreground objects), not motion blur. OBSERVED: The left and right edge strips are softer than the centre in 24-61 % of frames (median 35 %), edge sharpness 0.41-0.73 of the centre. Sharpness during a flight is the same as during a hold (ratio 1.05). WHY: A soft near object at the edge pushes the subject back in depth and costs nothing while the camera moves. DO: Put an out-of-focus foreground object (post, rope, leaf, rail, shoulder) at the left or right edge in about a third of the shots. Keep edge sharpness 0.4-0.7 of centre sharpness. No global motion blur. NUMBERS: edge_over_centre_sharpness 0.4078-0.7256 (median 0.646); frames_with_soft_edges 0.2444-0.6086 (median 0.351); flight_peak_sharpness_over_median 0.8884-1.1956 (median 1.049). SEEN IN: 17 references (kit/reference/look/_summary.json). [applies: universal] (ours now: edge 0.82 of centre, soft edges in 20 % of frames)
- [CAM-16 | proposed | for: any] Every camera choice has a written purpose, and a HOLD is a choice too. There is no default of moving and no default of holding. WHY: ChatGPT said hold-first; our measurements show 15-24 flights per minute. Purpose-first satisfies both: the mix comes out of the purposes. DO: Write the purpose first: establish, reveal, follow, inspect, emphasize, compare, land_on_prop, power_angle, hold_for_performance, carry_to_next_place, impact. Then pick the move (or static). A move needs a start view, an end view, a duration and an ease; a hold needs a reason (CAM-13). Keep the mix of CAM-01 (flights 27-54 % of the time) as the reference; do not force more stillness or more motion than the story needs. SEEN IN: chatgpt U06, U07, U12; our CAM-01, CAM-13 (measured mix). [applies: universal] (ours now: camera keys in story.js have no purpose; Gemini writes a free-text camera line per shot.)

### CUTS
- [CUT-01 | measured | for: any] Hard cuts are rare: a few per minute. The camera and dissolves carry most scene changes (see CUT-02). DO: 2-15 hard cuts per minute, median 7. Do not cut just to change the angle: fly the camera instead. Use a hard cut for a new place, a new time, or a change of topic. NUMBERS: hard_cuts_per_min p10 1.8 / median 6.6 / p90 14.64 (min 0.0, max 17.9); long_takes vp3: 0 hard cuts in 45 s, yet 13 scene changes made by dissolves and fly-throughs (see CUT-02). SEEN IN: 17 references. [applies: universal] (ours now: 58 per minute)
- [CUT-02 | measured | for: any, transition] The PLACE or set-up changes about every 2.4 seconds (18-24 times a minute). Four of every five scene changes are made WITHOUT a hard cut. WHY: Fast change of place keeps attention. A fly-through or a dissolve changes the place while the viewer's eye stays with the moving picture, so it feels smooth, not choppy. DO: Change scene every 2-3 s, 18-24 times per minute. Make the change with: dissolve (43 % of changes), camera fly-through (22 %), hard cut (21 %), in-place change (12 %), whip (2 %). Keep the camera moving inside the scene; do not cut for a new angle (see CUT-03). NUMBERS: scene_changes_per_min p10 18.34 / median 20.4 / p90 23.64 (min 16.0, max 24.9); mean over videos 20.9; gap_between_scene_changes_s average 2.75, median 2.43; type_share {'hard_cut': 0.21, 'dissolve': 0.43, 'whip': 0.02, 'camera_move': 0.22, 'in_place': 0.12}; counter_accuracy precision 0.84, recall 0.84 against 43 hand-labelled changes in 4 videos (first 30 s). SEEN IN: 17 references (per-video table: kit/reference/knowledge/transition_audit.json); hand check: scene_truth.json. [applies: universal] (ours now: 28 per minute, all hard cuts)
- [CUT-03 | measured | for: any] Do not cut to a new angle inside the same scene. Stay in the place and move the camera. WHY: The references hold one world for about 2 s and fly through it; every extra cut inside the scene breaks the 3D space the viewer just understood. DO: Hard cuts inside one scene: about 1 per minute at most (references median 1.1). A hard cut must land on a NEW place or a new beat of the script, never just a new angle of the same set. NUMBERS: ours_hard_cuts_per_min 58.2; ours_hard_cuts_inside_a_scene_per_min 25.0; references_hard_cuts_inside_a_scene_per_min_median 1.1; references_hard_cuts_per_min 1.8-14.6. SEEN IN: claude_bomb_v21 against 17 references. [applies: universal] (ours now: 25 per minute inside scenes)

### TRANSITIONS
- [TRN-01 | measured | for: transition] Carry the viewer to the next beat with the camera: fly through, into or under the next place. Do NOT add heavy blur: measured sharpness at the flight peak is the same as at a hold. DO: End a flight pointing at the next location, start the next beat already moving. Motion blur is at most slight: sharpness at flight peak / median sharpness is 0.89-1.20 (median 1.05). NUMBERS: flight_peak_sharpness_over_median 0.8884-1.1956 (median 1.049). SEEN IN: memory_price 4-8 s (alley, light-lined corridor, shop interior in one move); perfect_railroads 7-10 s (bridge, blur, station). [applies: universal]
- [TRN-02 | seen | for: transition, time_passes, emotion_shift] Cross-dissolve 4-10 frames, with a ghost of the old picture, for memory, thought, time shift or a change of speaker. DO: Overlap both pictures at 50 % for 2-3 frames. SEEN IN: memory_price 42-46 s (ghost of the hooded buyer over the boy); mirror_horse_race 3 s and 27 s; second_draw 13.6 s (dissolve to the quick-draw man). [applies: universal]
- [TRN-03 | seen | for: transition] Round masks: spyglass circle on black for looking at something far, round windows as frames, a black circle closing as an eye. DO: Use rarely, once or twice per short, for a view-through or a turning point. SEEN IN: mirror_horse_race 18 s (spyglass on the race); second_draw 44-53 s (black circle, then round windows). [applies: universal]
- [TRN-04 | seen | for: transition, action_impact] Smoke or cloud wipe: a puff fills the frame, the next place is behind it. DO: Smoke grows over 6-10 frames, clears into the new scene. SEEN IN: pirate_cannonballs 17.5-18.5 s (cannon smoke to open sea). [applies: universal]
- [TRN-05 | measured | for: transition, new_place] Most scene changes are either a fly-through (the camera passes into the next place) or a short cross-dissolve where both places show for a moment. WHY: Both keep the picture moving across the change, so the viewer does not feel a jump. DO: Dissolve when the next place is far away in space or time: the old picture ghosts through the new one for about 0.2-0.4 s (6-12 frames, read on 0.1 s strips). Fly-through when the next place is next door: the camera ends pointing at a door, street or panel, and the next shot starts already moving. NUMBERS: dissolve_share_of_scene_changes 0.43; dissolve_per_min_range 3.8-14.7 per video; camera_move_share 0.22. SEEN IN: vp3 10 s, 16 s, 24 s (dissolves between prize hall, counter and street); random_numbers 10-11 s (ghost of the tower over the office); knight_loophole 24 s; vp3 2-5 s (neon street seen from above, camera drops to the door); strips at 0.1 s: grave_bell 10.1-10.3 s, 13.3-13.5 s, vp3 10.4-10.5 s. [applies: universal]
- [TRN-06 | measured | for: transition, any] Mix the ways of changing scene. Dissolve is the default, a fly-through is the second choice, a hard cut is a choice for a new topic or a surprise. OBSERVED: Scene changes in 17 references: 43 % dissolve, 22 % camera fly-through, 21 % hard cut, 12 % in-place (prop or flash), 2 % whip. Ours: 100 % hard cut. WHY: The viewer keeps one continuous moving picture; a hard cut every 2 s feels like a slideshow. DO: Per minute (median video): about 9 dissolves, 5-6 camera fly-throughs, 3-4 hard cuts, 2 in-place changes, 0 whips (whip is rare: 0-2 per minute). Dissolve = 6-12 frames. Fly-through = the camera enters a door, tunnel, window, furnace, panel or street that is the next place. In-place = the prop or light changes while the camera rests (flash, turning a page, light switching on). NUMBERS: hard_cut_per_min 0-11 per video; dissolve_per_min 3.8-14.7 per video; camera_move_per_min 0-8.4 per video; whip_per_min 0-1.9 per video; in_place_per_min 0-6.1 per video. SEEN IN: kit/reference/knowledge/transition_audit.json (per video); pirate_cannonballs 23.05 s (fly into the furnace); perfect_railroads 21.3-21.7 s (whip pan then dissolve). [applies: universal] (ours now: 100 % hard cut)

### STORY SHAPE
- [END-01 | seen | for: ending] End with a callback: return to the first place or object, changed. DO: Last shot repeats the opening place or prop, with the final idea visible on it. SEEN IN: second_draw 54-55 s (street scene like the opening); town_button 64-65 s (crowd around the button from the first shot).

### SCRIPT TO PICTURE
- [SCR-01 | seen | for: any] One idea per sentence, one picture per idea. New place or angle at every sentence, new face or prop at every clause. DO: Narration runs about 2.5-3 words a second, captions show 1-3 words. NUMBERS: voice_onsets_per_s 2.8-3.5. SEEN IN: 8 references.
- [SCR-02 | seen | for: any] Show every important noun. Turn abstract ideas into an object: memory = ticket and shelves of boxes, happiness = gauge, time = ledger of years, rules = a button under glass. DO: List the nouns of each sentence before planning the shot and check each one appears. SEEN IN: memory_price; town_button; mirror_horse_race.
- [SCR-03 | seen | for: hook] Hook in the first 2-3 seconds: a face reacts, the main prop or place is in frame, and the first flight starts within the first second. DO: First fast flight starts at frame 1-27 (0.03-0.9 s) in 7 of 8 references; 2 of them start at frame 1-3. SEEN IN: pirate_cannonballs 0 s; second_draw 0 s; memory_price 0 s.

### CAPTIONS
- [CAP-01 | seen | for: any] Captions: bold white, thick black outline, centred at about 70 % of frame height, 1-3 words at a time, changing with the voice. DO: Keep the caption band free of important detail. SEEN IN: 8 references. [applies: universal]
- [CAP-02 | measured | for: any] Burn in captions: one spoken word at a time, big white text with a dark outline, centred low, popping in. OBSERVED: One word at a time, 1.928-2.592 (median 2.39) words per second, each word stays about 0.33-0.382 (median 0.37) s, shown 100 % of the time, centred at 0.6758-0.704 (median 0.699) of the frame height. A word is about 3-4 % of the frame height and 25-30 % of the frame width. It pops: the first 3 frames are 1.0292-1.206 (median 1.113) times the steady height. WHY: Viewers watch without sound; one word at a time keeps the eye on the centre of the screen. DO: One word per caption, shown from the word's start to the next word's start (about 0.37 s). Position: centred horizontally, centre at 70 % of the frame height. Height of a one-word caption about 3.5 % of the frame height; white fill, dark outline about 15 % of the letter height. Pop: start 10-15 % larger and settle to normal within 3 frames. NUMBERS: words_per_s 1.928-2.592 (median 2.39); word_on_screen_s 0.33-0.382 (median 0.37); centre_y 0.6758-0.704 (median 0.699); pop 1.0292-1.206 (median 1.113); clean_word_height_over_frame_h 0.030-0.039 (8 videos). SEEN IN: 17 references. (ESTIMATE NOTE: text height is reliable only in videos where the caption box is a single word (8 of 17); in the others white scenery in the band inflates it) [applies: universal] (ours now: our engine draws no captions)

Shakes: lift 0.722-1.372 (median 0.99). WHY: The voice has a new onset every 0.4 s, so onset alignment is automatic; what viewers notice is that the thing named is on screen. ### COMPOSITION
- [CMP-01 | proposed | for: any] Declare the composition of every shot: one primary subject, secondary context, a focal point, and a caption-clear zone. WHY: The planner and the preview check need a place to measure from. DO: Primary subject and hero object must be readable at phone size (about 360 px wide). Keep key content out of the caption band: captions sit at about 70 % of frame height (CAP-01), so the default clear zone is x 0.1-0.9, y 0.62-0.78. Put the focal point where the viewer should look after the camera lands (rule of thirds is a start, not a rule). SEEN IN: chatgpt U08. [applies: universal] (ours now: none: composition is implicit in camera keys; nothing declares or checks it.)

### CONTINUITY (identity lock)
- [CON-01 | proposed | for: any] Lock each character, object and place once, and keep it the same in every beat unless the script changes it. WHY: Identity from headwear and clothes (CHR-02) only works if it does not drift between shots. DO: Write an identity lock per character: head shape, hat, outfit colours, skin, beard, outline weight, size. Keep scale, screen side (who stands left or right) and position between beats of one place; change them only in a beat that lists continuity_change. When a story changes a look on purpose (boss face turns purple, rail heats up) list it as continuity_change. SEEN IN: chatgpt U03, U25. [applies: universal] (ours now: cast is defined by Gemini in cast.js per project; nothing checks that beats keep it.)

### CHARACTER ACTING
- [ACT-01 | proposed | for: any] Play an action in order: attention (gaze), anticipation, action, contact, response, settle. Gaze leads the hand. WHY: FX-01 says anticipation, action, follow-through; this adds gaze and the contact and response steps. DO: Eyes move first to the target, then the arm, then the hand touches. Give the body a small wind-up before a big action and a settle after it. Keep small-talk beats quiet: blink, breath, a small gesture only when the words need it. Our kit has one face name per beat and fixed arm poses (no separate brow, pupil, mouth channels): use the closest face and pose, and say so. SEEN IN: chatgpt U04, U05. [applies: universal] (ours now: idle() and blinkAt() exist in kit/engine/motion.js; M.anticip exists; no gaze-leads-hand logic; one face channel only.)

### MATERIALS
- [MAT-01 | proposed | for: any] Each material has its own shape and shading language (see material_recipes M01-M07). WHY: Surfaces with real texture are a measured need (COL-02, WLD-02); this says which texture. DO: Wood: planks and seams with a grain direction. Metal: edge highlights and dark seams. Stone: block variation. Earth: layered strata and pebbles. Water: ripples and a bright glint. Foliage: clumps with value variation. Glass: reflection and a thin edge. Choose the materials per place in the beat plan (material_ids), not per shot. SEEN IN: chatgpt U14, M01-M07. [applies: universal] (ours now: toonbase/paint.js and the railroads_v2 world.js have texture helpers (woodTex, sandTex, gravelTex, strataTex in mine/railroads_v2/web/main.js); no material list in the kit.)
- [MAT-02 | proposed | for: any] Big forms first, then a few purposeful details. Do not add small noise everywhere. WHY: Detail should help the story, not hide it. DO: Silhouette and big structure must read first. Add 3-5 details per hero object that say what it is: seams, bolts, labels, bevels, grain, wear. SEEN IN: chatgpt U15. [applies: universal] (ours now: hand-built per project.)

### HOW THINGS ARE BUILT (2D / 2.5D / 3D)
- [ARC-01 | proposed | for: any] Choose how each thing is built by what the camera does to it: people are 2D cards in a 3D world, hero objects the camera moves around are 3D, far scenery can be flat layers, effects are billboards. WHY: Keeps cost and look under control. DO: Orbit or close-up on it -> 3D mesh. Always front-facing -> 2D card. Far and static -> 2.5D layer. Smoke, sparks, glow -> billboard fx. Write the representation per object in the beat plan. SEEN IN: chatgpt U02. [applies: universal] (ours now: our kit already works this way (roman.js cards in a three.js world); the choice is made by hand.)

### NEW TOPICS
- [ADP-01 | proposed | for: any] For a new topic keep the universal habits (PRF-01) and choose the topic things fresh: place, props, materials, light, motion. WHY: The goal is a toolkit for new topics, not a copy of 17 videos. DO: Never reuse a reference layout, prop set or shot order. Take the habit (how a reveal is built), not the picture. Pick the topic profile (PRF-02, PRF-03) by what the story does: machine, money, mind, night. SEEN IN: chatgpt U27; our PRF-01..03. [applies: universal] (ours now: tested once: Why Perfect Railroads Don't Work (railroads_v2) from words only.)

### CHECK BEFORE RENDERING
- [QC-01 | proposed | for: any] Check before you render: make a small preview of every beat and judge it against the quality gates, then fix or reject bad beats before the full render. WHY: A full render costs minutes to hours; a preview costs seconds. DO: One low-resolution frame per beat (start, middle, end) in a contact sheet. Run the gates Q01-Q10 (rules.json quality_gates): some are automatic, some need Gemini vision, some need a person. Do not start a full render while a gate marked automatic fails. SEEN IN: chatgpt U26, Q01-Q10. [applies: universal] (ours now: partly: tools/gen_api.py renders 3 stills per shot and asks Gemini for PASS/FAIL (Gemini projects only, does not use beats or the gates Q01-Q10). frame_qa.py, ref_measure.py compare and ref_study.py compare run only AFTER the full render.)

## Beat intents and shot recipes (choose per beat; candidates, not a fixed order)

Give every beat an INTENT (what the words do). Candidate recipes are scored against the assets, the previous beat and CAM-10 (vary the moves). A camera move or hold always needs a purpose (CAM-16).

- hook: show First 2-3 s: a reacting face or the hero object in frame, first flight inside 1 s. Recipes: S04, S03, S05. Rules: SCR-03, CAM-04, CAM-02.
- introduce_place_or_time: show Environment, a scale anchor and one key prop. Recipes: S01, S05. Rules: CAM-04, WLD-01, WLD-03.
- introduce_character: show The character readable by hat and clothes, expression first. Recipes: S02, S04. Rules: CHR-02, FAC-01, CAM-08.
- explain_mechanism: show The hero object, its moving part and the cause and effect state. Recipes: S03, S07, S06. Rules: PRP-05, WLD-06, CAM-05.
- give_number_or_quantity: show A large legible value on a prop plus context for scale. Recipes: S03, S07. Rules: PRF-04, PRP-01, PRP-03, CAM-05.
- physical_action: show Actor, object and the destination or impact. Recipes: S06, S03. Rules: PHY-03, FX-01, FX-02, CAM-07.
- create_suspense: show One clear focal point, controlled information, a slow creep or a hold. Recipes: S03, S04, S07. Rules: CAM-13, CAM-06, LIT-06.
- surprising_reveal: show Before and after composition: start tight or on a reaction, widen to the truth. Recipes: S05, S04. Rules: CAM-04, CAM-11.
- emotional_reaction: show Face pose plus the trigger object. Recipes: S04, S02. Rules: FAC-01, FAC-02, CAM-08.
- dialogue_or_argument: show Two characters, reaction faces, held camera. Recipes: S08, S04. Rules: CAM-08, CAM-13, CON-01.
- time_passes: show A clock, calendar, season or light change; a dissolve. Recipes: S07, S01. Rules: TRN-02, PRP-03, LIT-03.
- comedic_beat: show Land a hard beat, then the gag picture with a small motion. Recipes: S04, S06. Rules: PHY-02, FAC-02.
- crowd_or_scale: show Hundreds of tiny varied people or a huge object against a person. Recipes: S05, S01. Rules: WLD-05, CAM-11.
- summarize_or_conclude: show Return to the first place or object, changed. Recipes: S01, S02, S05. Rules: END-01.

- S01 Establishing world (1.5-3.5 s, designed): Orient viewer to location, scale and key objects. Framing: wide or medium-wide; clear horizon / ground plane; one obvious focal point. Camera: hold or slow purposeful pan/dolly only if it reveals geography (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason). Needs: environment, scale anchor, one key prop. Fits: introduce_place_or_time, crowd_or_scale, summarize_or_conclude, time_passes.
- S02 Narrator character hold (1.0-3.5 s, designed): Let the narration land while maintaining character presence. Framing: medium / medium-wide; character readable; supporting set dressing. Camera: locked or nearly locked (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason). Needs: consistent character, role costume or accessory. Fits: introduce_character, emotional_reaction, summarize_or_conclude.
- S03 Object / mechanism insert (0.6-2.0 s, designed): Explain a mechanism, detail or evidence. Framing: close-up, top-down, POV or cutaway; object fills enough of frame to read. Camera: locked, short push or tracking move that follows the mechanism (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason). Needs: hero object, moving part, cause and effect state. Fits: explain_mechanism, give_number_or_quantity, create_suspense, hook, physical_action.
- S04 Character reaction close-up (0.5-1.5 s, designed): Emphasize recognition, fear, surprise, confidence or realization. Framing: head / upper body; eyebrows, pupils and mouth readable. Camera: cut to close-up or short push; avoid continuous generic zoom (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason). Needs: face pose, trigger object. Fits: emotional_reaction, hook, create_suspense, comedic_beat, dialogue_or_argument, surprising_reveal.
- S05 Scale reveal / pullback (1.0-3.0 s, designed): Reveal crowd, full machine, geography or surprising scale. Framing: start with partial/close view; end with the full subject/context visible. Camera: crane / dolly back / zoom only if perspective is not needed; use parallax when possible (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason). Needs: reveal target, before and after composition. Fits: surprising_reveal, crowd_or_scale, introduce_place_or_time.
- S06 Action demonstration (1.0-3.0 s, designed): Show how an action works and its consequence. Framing: wide enough to understand actor, prop and destination; insert details where needed. Camera: track/follow only if subject travels; maintain screen direction (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason). Needs: actor, object, destination or impact. Fits: physical_action, comedic_beat.
- S07 Diagrammatic metaphor / cutaway (1.0-2.5 s, designed): Make abstract ideas visible. Framing: clean isolated diagram or transparent/cutaway body/object; simple composition. Camera: hold or subtle drift; avoid busy movement (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason). Needs: diagram or cutaway, legible values. Fits: explain_mechanism, give_number_or_quantity, time_passes, create_suspense.
- S08 Two-character dialogue (1.0-3.0 s, designed): Show an exchange or contrast. Framing: balanced two-shot; both faces readable; props placed between/near them. Camera: hold; change to close-up only when reaction matters (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason). Needs: two characters, reaction face. Fits: dialogue_or_argument, emotional_reaction.

## Materials and light profiles (checklists from the independent study, not measured)

- M01 painted_wood: shape planks, beams, posts, boards with clear seams and slightly softened edges; surface subtle grain direction, value variation, occasional knots/wear; do not over-noise; light broad warm highlight and soft contact shadow.
- M02 painted_metal: shape simple bevelled plates, rims, bolts, hinges, rods and cylindrical forms; surface clean base colour, edge highlight, controlled roughness and small scratches; light directional specular highlight; stronger rim on round objects.
- M03 stone_brick_masonry: shape large readable blocks, irregular joints, bevelled corners; surface few hue/value shifts per block, restrained noise and shadow in seams; light directional light to reveal block depth.
- M04 earth_sand_rock: shape layered ground planes, clumps, stones and uneven edges; surface clustered colour patches, sparse pebbles, broad value variation; light warm directional sunlight and contact shadows.
- M05 water: shape large coherent planes with wave silhouettes, reflections and foam accents; surface directional ripple bands; highlights follow wave direction; avoid random white noise; light environment reflection, blue/cyan palette shifts and brighter glints.
- M06 foliage_grass: shape clustered leaf/grass silhouettes; vary scale and density by depth; surface controlled hue/value variation and layered shadow patches; light light through canopy, not uniform green fill.
- M07 glass: shape simple transparent planes, bevels and clear frame edges; surface selective reflections/highlights; keep contents readable; light bright edge glints and restrained transparency.
- L01 warm_interior: palette amber, ochre, warm cream, wood brown; controlled saturated accents; key motivated lamp/window key; fill moderate, keep face readable; shadow soft but directional contact shadows; use for shops, workshops, cabins, historical interiors.
- L02 bright_daylight: palette clear sky blue, green, warm earth, high-value character heads; key broad directional sun; fill sky fill; shadow visible direction and ground contact; use for towns, fields, railways, coaster parks.
- L03 cool_night_storm: palette deep blue, indigo, violet, teal with warm practical lights; key moon/sky or motivated lantern; fill low; preserve character silhouette; shadow stronger contrast and selective rim; use for night streets, ships, graveyard, storms.
- L04 dramatic_hero_prop: palette restrained environment plus warm/cool accent on hero object; key spotlight, practical glow or emissive source; fill low-to-moderate; shadow object contact and local occlusion; use for machines, gauges, cannonballs, important buttons.

## Recipes by situation (shot plans)

- HOOK (0-3 s): 1) First flight starts within 1 s. 2) Close on a reacting face, main prop or place visible. 3) First flight ends on the hero object by 1.5-3 s. Rules: SCR-03, CAM-04, CAM-02.
- NEW_PLACE (2-4 s): 1) Start tight on a detail or face. 2) Fly out, up or around 0.8-1.6 s with ease in and out. 3) End on a wide with the hero object, a far landmark and 6-10 dressing pieces. 4) Hold 0.5-1 s. Rules: CAM-04, WLD-01, WLD-02, WLD-03, LIT-02.
- INTRODUCE_CHARACTER (1.5-3 s): 1) Medium shot, character readable by hat and clothes. 2) Expression first, then a prop in the hand. 3) Slow creep. Rules: CHR-01, CHR-02, FAC-01, CAM-08.
- KEY_PROP (1-2 s): 1) Fast push that decelerates onto the prop on the word. 2) Prop fills 40-100 % of the frame, text readable. 3) Light effect on it (glow, glass highlight, bloom). Rules: CAM-05, PRP-01, PRP-02, LIT-04.
- DIALOGUE (1.5-4 s): 1) Two-shot or close-up held. 2) Camera creeps under 8 % per second. 3) Face changes every 1-1.5 s. Rules: CAM-08, FAC-01.
- ACTION_IMPACT (1-2.5 s): 1) Anticipation hold 0.6 s. 2) Push to the point of action with streaks or starburst. 3) Debris 0.5-1 s. 4) Pull back, bystander reaction within 0.2 s. Rules: FX-01, FX-02, FX-03, PHY-01, CAM-05.
- EXPLAIN_SYSTEM (3-5 s): 1) Crane to top-down to show the layout. 2) Draw the idea in the world (ring, arcs, numbers). 3) Come back down to a character reacting. Rules: CAM-04, PRP-05.
- EMOTION_SHIFT (1-3 s): 1) Change the colour grade on the cut or the dissolve. 2) Face shows the new feeling with its effect (steam, sweat, tears). Rules: LIT-03, FAC-02, TRN-02.
- TIME_PASSES (1-2 s): 1) Dissolve with ghost. 2) Show a clock, calendar, ledger or season change. 3) Light changes with the time. Rules: TRN-02, PRP-03.
- CROWD (2-3 s): 1) Wide from low or high. 2) Hundreds of tiny varied people in rows, bunting, a few animated. 3) Cut or fly to one face in the crowd. Rules: WLD-05, CAM-11.
- DANGER (1.5-3 s): 1) Low angle, big prop in the foreground. 2) Hard long shadows, orange low light. 3) Hold, then a sudden push. Rules: CAM-06, LIT-03.
- COMEDY_GAG (1-2 s): 1) Land a hard beat first (impact, fall, reveal). 2) Cut or push to the gag picture: knocked-out face stamped in a sand ring, exaggerated stare, size contrast. 3) Hold 1-1.5 s with only a small motion (dust settling, eye twitch). Rules: PHY-02, PHY-01, FAC-02.
- ENDING (2-4 s): 1) Return to the first place or object. 2) Slow pull back, final line on the prop or a face. Rules: END-01.
- NUMBER_DATA (4-7 s): 1) Medium shot, character beside the big number prop, camera holds (CAM-13). 2) On the key word push toward the prop and land on it with the number readable (CAM-05). 3) The number changes on the spoken word (counter rolls, panel light turns on). 4) Fly out or up to show what the number means in the world (skyline, crowd, line of people). Rules: CAM-13, CAM-05, PRP-01, PRF-04.

## ENGINE (what our renderer does with these rules)
- implemented from these rules: nothing yet. Nothing from rules.json is wired into kit/engine yet. v2.2 (bomb story) tests whether the rules help when applied by hand in story.js. Update this list only when code reads a rule or a number.
- gap: no burned-in captions at all (references show one word at a time for 100 % of the time)
- gap: scene changes are 100 % hard cuts: no dissolve, no fly-through scene change
- gap: 25 hard cuts per minute inside scenes (references median 1.1)
- gap: surfaces too flat: 60 % flat colour, 5.6 % smooth gradient (references 35-48 % and 14-20 %)
- gap: heads small: 13 % of frame height (references 12-21 %, median 17 %) and skin-coloured, not near-white
- gap: shake: 35 events per minute that die in 0.03 s (references 3-20 per minute, 0.12-0.28 s)
- gap: camera ease: ramp-up 0.17 s, no long ease-out (references ramp-up 0.28 s, ramp-down 0.47 s)

## Quality gates (before the full render, QC-01)
- Q01 Character identity: Head proportions, face placement, costume, outline and accessories remain consistent across planned shots. Checks: [automatic] character ids, outfit, hat and identity_lock are the same in every beat; [ai_assisted] head, face, costume look the same across the preview frames; [human] final approval of the look
- Q02 Composition: One primary focal subject; key action and hero object readable at phone scale; caption safe zone does not obscure critical content. Checks: [automatic] the focal point is not inside the caption clear zone (warning); the zone defaults to the measured caption band; [ai_assisted] hero object and action readable at phone size in the preview frames; [human] does the picture say what the words say
- Q03 Camera intent: Every non-static move has a written purpose, target, direction, duration and easing. HOLD is allowed. Checks: [automatic] every beat has a camera purpose and mode; a move has duration, ease and from/to; a hold has a rationale; [human] the move helps the story
- Q04 Narration match: Every sentence/beat has an explicit visual purpose and subject; no generic filler shots. Checks: [automatic] beat words joined equal the narration; word ranges cover all words in order; beat times follow the word times; [ai_assisted] each named noun is visible within 0.3 s of its word (CHK-07)
- Q05 Physics causality: Object has initial state, action/force, trajectory, contact/response and settled state; no teleporting or weightless motion. Checks: [automatic] physical events name a contact target and fitting secondary effects; [human] the motion looks causal and has weight
- Q06 Environment depth: Foreground/midground/background, scale cues, contact shadows and perspective relationships are present where relevant. Checks: [automatic] every environment declares foreground, midground, background; [automatic] parallax and soft-edge share on rendered frames
- Q07 Material readability: Wood/metal/stone/water/cloth/glass read differently by geometry and shading, not colour alone. Checks: [automatic] every declared material id exists in material_recipes; [ai_assisted] the surface reads as that material in the preview
- Q08 Edit purpose: Cuts and transitions correspond to semantic changes; adjacent shots do not repeat the same information. Checks: [automatic] every beat has a transition type and reason (frames for dissolve, fly-through, flash); hard cuts at most 45 % of scene changes (CHK-11) and at least one dissolve (warnings); [human] each cut is on a meaning beat
- Q09 Audio events: SFX are linked to named visual events, and narration remains intelligible over music. Checks: [automatic] audio events have a valid trigger and fall inside the beat; word triggers point at real words; [automatic] mix level and loudness; [human] sound quality and taste
- Q10 Render preflight: Low-resolution animatic and contact sheet reviewed before a full-resolution render. Checks: [automatic] all ids resolve; every required asset is declared; beats cover the whole video without gaps or overlaps; [automatic] a build check of the real code (assets render, no errors)

## Checks (run on a finished video)
- CHK-01: hard cuts per minute should be 1.8 .. 14.6 (python3 kit/tools/ref_study.py compare video.mp4)
- CHK-08: scene changes per minute (new place or set-up, incl. dissolves) should be 18.3 .. 23.6 (same)
- CHK-09: hard cuts should be well below scene changes (angle cuts inside a scene) (compare the two numbers above)
- CHK-02: share of shots that are only a zoom should be 0 .. 0.07 (same)
- CHK-03: share of time the picture moves fast should be 0.27 .. 0.54 (same)
- CHK-04: depth parallax in flights should be 0.32 .. 0.44 (same)
- CHK-05: palette size (4-bit colours over 0.5 %) should be 32 .. 45 (python3 kit/tools/ref_measure.py compare video.mp4)
- CHK-06: frame-to-frame change (median) should be 3.6 .. 9.5 (same)
- CHK-07: script match: every noun of each sentence appears within 0.3 s of the word (manual until the script-match check is built (step 2))
- CHK-10: hard cuts that are not scene changes, per minute should be 0 .. 3 (python3 kit/tools/ref_transitions.py audit (hard_cuts_inside_a_scene_per_min))
- CHK-11: share of scene changes that are hard cuts should be 0.0 .. 0.45 (same (by_type_share))
- CHK-12: flat-colour share of the picture should be 0.3498 .. 0.4774 (python3 kit/tools/ref_look.py study video.mp4 --name X --group ours)
- CHK-13: captions on screen (share of time) should be 0.95 .. 1.0 (same)

## Limits of this knowledge
- 17 camera-studied videos, all in one house style (3D world, 2D bean-head cards, one-word captions). Another genre may need other values.
- Topic groups (history/war 6, money-gamble-crime 6, engineering 3, science-mind 1, night-horror 1) are Claude's labels. PRELIMINARY: groups of 1 to 3 are single examples, not ranges.
- Scene counter: precision 0.84, recall 0.84 on 43 changes labelled by eye in 4 videos (first 30 s). Type labels: 5 of 6 spot checks right. Treat counts as about +-20 %. Angle changes inside a scene are not counted as scene changes.
- 3 of the videos (vp3, vp4, vp5) are 360x640; the rest 720x1280. Our v2.1 is 1080x1920. All measures are ratios.
- Head finder works on clean near-white heads only; eyes are measured only where open dots are visible; limb thickness separate from outline, body proportions, material types and physics trajectories are NOT measured (no reliable way from a flat video).
- Caption text height is reliable in 8 of 17 videos (single word in a clean band); the rest are inflated by white scenery.
- Sound: only loudness (-14 LUFS) and onset alignment (none beyond chance) are known. Music, voice and sound effects cannot be separated from the mixed track.
- The 6 older reference videos are in the colour database but NOT in the camera study (their video files were not kept).
- No script text for the references. Script-to-picture rules come from reading the captions on the frames.
- These rules are NOT read by the render code. They reach Gemini only through the PLAYBOOK in its prompt (untested).
- Rules with conf "proposed" (15 rules, merged 2026-11-08 from an independent ChatGPT study) were not measured or seen by us and have not been applied in a video yet.

## How this grows
Add a reference: `python3 kit/tools/ref_study.py study video.mp4 --name NAME --group refs`, `python3 kit/tools/ref_measure.py add video.mp4 --name NAME --group refs`, `python3 kit/tools/ref_sheet.py video.mp4 kit/reference/study/NAME.json /tmp/NAME` (look at the sheets), `python3 kit/tools/ref_study.py rules`, add or correct rules in kit/reference/knowledge/rules.json (keep conf honest, give times as evidence), then `python3 kit/tools/build_playbook.py`. Log it in kit/reference/knowledge/LEARNING_LOG.md.
